newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Fernandez considers IMF stand-by deal.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez considers IMF stand-by deal.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez was quoted Tuesday as saying he may now settle for just a stand-by agreement with the International Monetary fund rather than a more encompassing Extended Fund Facility.

"The thing is that a stand-by agreement only includes fiscal targets. On the other hand, the other agreement (Extended Fund Facility) also includes structural reforms," Fernandez said in an interview with daily La Nacion.
Fernandez had previously said Argentina was negotiating with the IMF for an Extended Fund Facility.

"For example: we could include labor reform, but we have to put down a date. And how do you do that? Because there is a negotiating table and it is also being dealt with by the courts. How can we put a timetable on the courts?," he said.
The government decreed several measures to make the labor market more flexible in December, but they were challenged as being unconstitutional.

The decree included allowing workers to choose their own union health plan, letting smaller firms bypass national unions in collective pay talks, and allowing firms to appeal to the government if they want to negotiate with unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.

Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa said on the weekend that the government may now wait until after the October mid-term congressional elections to push ahead with the reforms facing the most opposition.
"In these types of agreements, one cannot include expressions of what one wants but clear targets with timetables," Fernandez said.
However, the minister did not rule out either agreement. He said the two options are a three-year stand-by agreement or a three-year Extended Fund Facility.
Argentina's current stand-by accord with the IMF that ends this year includes a deficit target of $3 billion for 1997. Argentina met the first quarter target with a deficit of $1.04 billion.
